title: What happened in AI — Aug 5, 2026
intro: Agent security moved from proposal to practice: Cloudflare published a formal access-control architecture for task-scoped agents the same day researchers reported China-linked actors using DeepSeek to orchestrate attempted attacks on Hermes agents, while two new open-source projects shipped sandboxes for isolating agent execution.

The coding-agent field also widened — Meta joined with persistent async background agents and DeepSeek confirmed its own coding agent is coming — as China's AI stack absorbed pressure on multiple fronts, from a ByteDance distillation ban to a reported US components import ban.
highlights: Cloudflare proposed a formal Agent Access Model for identity brokering and continuous trust, right as researchers reported DeepSeek-orchestrated attacks on Hermes agents.
Meta entered the coding-agent race with Muse Spark 1.2 and Muse Code's persistent async background agents; DeepSeek confirmed its own coding agent is coming.
AWS and LangChain both shipped production agent infra: an MCP bridge from cloud agents to local tools, and an autonomous Kubernetes SRE agent gated on human approval.
ByteDance banned employees from distilling US models the same day Anthropic confirmed a custom Claude chip, while DeepSeek V4 Flash topped OpenRouter's weekly usage ranking.
A viral claim that Ponytail cuts agent-generated code 80-94% got corrected after a contributor showed the benchmark's baseline was flawed.
